findings.passage: “The poll released today by F&M shows that 73% of Pennsylvanians support requiring a photo identification each time someone goes to vote.
findings.note: Caucus release in his name. He cites a poll and backs a petition to bring a voter ID constitutional amendment to a House vote.

findings.passage: “If this amendment gets approved by the General Assembly by early July, it would be in a position to be considered on the ballot during the November General Election – a high turnout election that would ensure maximum voter participation on this important question,” Cutler said.
findings.note: He sets a timeline to put the voter ID amendment before voters in November 2024.

findings.passage: “Commonsense tells us that as more and more proposals are introduced to make our elections harder to administer and less secure, that simply requiring a state-provided identification at each election is the best way to enhance election integrity.
findings.note: Quoted at a House caucus press conference announcing the discharge petition. He describes a state-provided ID at each election. Page published 2024-03-26; press conference was the Monday before.

findings.passage: “With 100 signatures on the voter identification constitutional amendment discharge petition, it is clear House Democrats need to get out of their own way and put up this easily achievable election reform for a vote in the House,” Cutler said.
findings.note: He presses for a floor vote on the voter ID amendment. The same release also mentions signature verification on mail ballots and pre-canvassing.

findings.passage: “As we are now a week from Election Day, these ongoing issues make it clearer than ever that the most universal answer to many of today’s election integrity questions is requiring voters to show identification at each and every election.”
findings.note: Statement on county voter-registration fraud investigations; he ties them to ID at every election. Also mentions the 2021 Voting Rights Protection Act vetoed by the governor, which he says included enhanced voter identification.

findings.passage: “Voters deserve the opportunity to make some of these changes on their own, which is why a bipartisan majority of both chambers supported constitutional amendments to reform Pennsylvania’s post-election auditing process, and voter identification requirements.
findings.note: Statement as Speaker after a court ruling on Act 77 (mail voting). He supports voter ID and audit amendments going to voters.

findings.passage: Rep. Bryan Cutler (R., Lancaster) challenged that assessment, calling the bill "a move to ensure the constitutional guarantee of one person, one vote."
findings.note: Inquirer quote on the 2011 House photo ID bill; only the quoted phrase is his own words, the rest is the reporter's sentence.
